security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU TCG translator uses incorrect sign-extension width for a Narrowing Clip instruction variant (e.g., sign_extend(64, ...) instead of sign_extend(48, ...) for PNCLIP.BS byte narrowing, or sign_extend(128, ...) instead of sign_extend(64, ...) for halfword narrowing variants). The spec requires distinct extension widths per element size: 48-bit for byte narrowing with scalar shift, 64-bit for halfword narrowing, and 128-bit for word (XLEN-wide) narrowing. If the translator reuses a generic helper with a fixed extension width, the arithmetic right shift produces incorrect saturation decisions — a value near the clip boundary could be misclassified as in-range or saturated, producing wrong output in rd and incorrect vxsat sticky flag state. Additionally, the shift-amount bit-width varies per variant (4-bit imm for byte, 5-bit for halfword, 6-bit for word narrowing); masking the wrong number of bits from the shift operand changes which bits participate, altering the shift amount and producing entirely different results.
security_spec.summary: Narrowing Clip instructions require variant-specific sign-extension widths (48/64/128-bit) and shift-amount bit-widths (4/5/6-bit); a generic TCG helper reusing a single width across variants would produce incorrect saturation and wrong rd/vxsat values

findings.finding: The P-extension (packed SIMD, Zpn/Zpng) including Narrowing Clip instructions (PNCLIP.BS, PNCLIP.HS, PNCLIP.WS, and their unsigned variants) is not implemented in QEMU's RISC-V target. No decode entries, translator functions, helper definitions, or TCG code exists for any P-extension packed SIMD instructions. The only 'clip' instructions present are the V-extension vector narrowing clip (vnclip*) in insn32.decode and vector_helper.c — these are distinct from the P-extension scalar packed SIMD narrowing clip instructions described in the security spec.
findings.snippet: N/A — no P-extension code exists in QEMU target/riscv/
